record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Let M = (g ⊗ A)^Γ be a perfect equivariant map Lie algebra, formed from a Lie algebra g, a coordinate algebra A of an affine scheme X, and a compatible Γ-action. Understand the central extensions of M, especially its universal central extension uce(M). Determine when the universal central extension of the fixed-point algebra agrees with the fixed points of the universal central extension of the untwisted algebra, that is, when uce((g ⊗ A)^Γ) is naturally isomorphic to uce(g ⊗ A)^Γ.

evidence.quote: The action of Γ on X induces an action on the coordinate ring A of X. Then M = (a ⊗ A)Γ , the fixed points of the diagonal action of Γ on a ⊗ A.

4.3.3. Central extensions. Central extensions of Lie algebras often have a sim- pler representation theory, the affine Kac-Moody Lie algebras being a case in point. It is therefore of interest to understand central extensions of equivariant map alge- bras M, preferably the universal central extension uce(M) of a perfect M.

Generalizing the example of twisted loop algebras, one would like to relate the universal central extension of a perfect equivariant map algebra (g ⊗ A)Γ to the well-understood universal central extension uce(g ⊗ A). Observe that the action of Γ on g ⊗ A uniquely lifts to an action on uce(g ⊗ A). The formula one is aiming for is then very natural: uce((g ⊗ A)Γ) ≃ uce(g ⊗ A)Γ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, let $X$ be an affine scheme of finite type over $k$ with coordinate algebra $A = k[X]$, and let $\Gamma$ be a finite group acting on $\mathfrak{g}$ by Lie algebra automorphisms and on $X$ by scheme automorphisms; let $\Gamma$ act diagonally on $\mathfrak{g} \otimes A$ (with the induced action on $A$). The equivariant map algebra is
$$ M = (\mathfrak{g} \otimes A)^{\Gamma}, $$
the fixed-point subalgebra of $\mathfrak{g} \otimes A$ under $\Gamma$. Assume $M$ is perfect, so its universal central extension $\mathrm{uce}(M)$ exists. The $\Gamma$-action on $\mathfrak{g} \otimes A$ lifts uniquely to an action on the universal central extension $\mathrm{uce}(\mathfrak{g} \otimes A)$.

Problem: Describe the central extensions of $M$, and in particular its universal central extension $\mathrm{uce}(M)$. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $(\mathfrak{g}, A, \Gamma)$ under which there is a natural isomorphism
$$ \mathrm{uce}\bigl((\mathfrak{g} \otimes A)^{\Gamma}\bigr) \;\cong\; \mathrm{uce}(\mathfrak{g} \otimes A)^{\Gamma}. $$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of relating the universal central extension of a perfect equivariant map algebra to the fixed points of the universal central extension of the underlying untwisted current algebra has been studied in special cases (e.g., twisted loop algebras, multiloop algebras, and certain twisted current algebras). General results have been obtained for various subclasses, but a complete characterization of when the natural isomorphism $\mathrm{uce}((\mathfrak{g} \otimes A)^{\Gamma}) \cong \mathrm{uce}(\mathfrak{g} \otimes A)^{\Gamma}$ holds for all perfect equivariant map algebras does not appear to have been fully established in the literature available via search.

status_evidence.title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
status_evidence.snippet: It is therefore of interest to understand central extensions of equivariant map algebras M, preferably the universal central extension uce(M) of a perfect M. ... The formula one is aiming for is then very natural: uce((g ⊗ A)^Γ) ≃ uce(g ⊗ A)^Γ.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether uce((g⊗A)^Γ) ≅ uce(g⊗A)^Γ is posed as an open direction.

status_evidence.title: Extensions of modules for twisted current algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Twisted current algebras are fixed point subalgebras of current algebras under a finite group action.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on twisted current algebras has addressed extension-theoretic questions but not a complete general isomorphism criterion.
